A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FedYoYo research work, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–C. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of all equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original FedYoYo experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations, and representation analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including Tables 1–6 and the experimental figures.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same augmented self-bootstrap distillation, distribution-aware logit adjustment, distribution fusion, combined loss, and FedAvg aggregation procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same classification coverage: CIFAR-10/100 under standard non-IID settings, CIFAR-10/100-LT, SVHN-LT, and ImageNet-LT. No dataset or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding Tables 1–3 and supplementary comparisons. The centralized, heterogeneity-oriented, distillation, imbalance-oriented, and federated long-tailed baselines are retained.

E3.justification: The reported Dirichlet parameters, imbalance factors, model architectures, 300-round training budget, accuracy metrics, class-group definitions, and ablation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain identical component and augmentation ablations, distribution-fusion and hyperparameter analyses, and global/local model and feature comparisons. Appendices B–C add or remove no analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the error-bar and band displays in Figures 9–10. No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported values and findings match. For example, Table 2 retains FedYoYo accuracies of 81.45% and 46.13% on CIFAR-10/100-LT at IF=100 and alpha=0.5; Table 3 retains 31.41% overall on ImageNet-LT.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, and mathematical formulation in Section 2, including Equations (1)–(9), are unchanged. No theoretical result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about approaching centralized performance, surpassing centralized baselines under global long tails, and improving representations through ASD and DLA.

C2.justification: Interpretations of client drift, feature alignment, distribution estimation, and component synergy are identical. Section 2.5 retains the same privacy discussion and qualifications concerning distribution sharing.

D1.justification: Both provide identical implementation disclosures, including PyTorch, NVIDIA GeForce 3090 GPUs, augmentation procedures, and hyperparameter information. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 4 and all 45 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to self-supervised learning, neural-collapse-inspired methods, and logit adjustment.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 10 March 2025 to v2 dated 25 September 2025. The paper's wording, headings, and section and appendix organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and six tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. Visual inspection confirms unchanged page layouts; negligible rendering differences do not alter the displays.

improvement.justification: The main paper and Appendices A–C retain the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information. The updated arXiv stamp and negligible typesetting differences produce no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
